Turdus migratorius: American Robin: clear, rising-and-falling caroling phrases; common on lawns and woodland edges, loudest at dawn and dusk.
Cardinalis cardinalis: Northern Cardinal: loud, clear whistles like 'cheer-cheer-cheer'; thickets and shrubby edges.
Poecile atricapillus: Black-capped Chickadee: whistled 'fee-bee' song and a buzzy 'chick-a-dee-dee-dee' call; mixed woodland.
Corvus corax: Common Raven: deep croaks and varied gurgles; cliffs, forests and open country.
Parus major: Great Tit: ringing 'tea-cher, tea-cher' song; woodland, parks and gardens.
Erithacus rubecula: European Robin: thin, liquid, wistful warbling; sings even in winter and at night near lights.
Turdus merula: Common Blackbird: rich, flute-like phrases at dusk and dawn; gardens and woods.
Strix varia: Barred Owl: 'who cooks for you, who cooks for you-all'; wet mature forest, active at dusk.
